How this affects stocks · sources & catalysts

Rising yields can lower equity valuations and raise financing costs. Falling yields can reflect easing inflation or weaker growth; the reason matters. Bond ETF prices alone do not establish a crisis.

These are ETF price returns, excluding distributions. HYG and LQD mix interest-rate and credit risk; neither is a direct credit-spread measure. UUP and USO are futures-fund proxies. Hover or tap through for the instrument chart. Daily closes, not intraday signals.

Indicator definitions

Simple moving averages use completed closes. RSI and ATR use 14-session Wilder smoothing. ATR measures range, not direction. Volume compares the last session with the preceding 20. Relative performance is the stock’s price return minus SPY’s over identical dates; dividends are excluded. The prior 20-session high uses closes and excludes the latest session. Indicators describe history and are not entry recommendations.

Method & coverage

One observation per politician, ticker and purchase date; repeated ownership rows count once. Excludes options, exercises, sales and local imports. Period filters purchase dates. Uses exact purchase-day or disclosure-day close; missing dates/prices remain unpriced. Different holding periods are not annualized. No dividends, fees, taxes or sale matching. Disclosure-day close may precede public release. Coverage is incomplete; the separately linked 2025 estimate is not used in these rankings.

Connecting to feeds…

poor checks feeds on opening, on returning to the tab and every 15 minutes while visible. Disclosure feeds are cached for 6 hours; price data for 15 minutes. Refreshing runs on the hosted website. There is no unattended scheduler: no visitors means no refresh until the next visit.

Last successful feeds are saved on the server. Errors trigger a 10-minute retry cooldown. A source check is not proof that the publisher released new filings. The Congress feed scans up to 5,000 latest rows from the last 365 days and retains only the five selected households, plus their historical seed records. Executive feeds are no longer displayed. Existing checked records take precedence when a feed covers the same document, person, ticker and date. Feed summaries are not independently verified; corrections rely on the providers.

Sources: CongressInvests · Open Cabinet · Yahoo Finance.

Roster selection · reviewed September 26, 2026

The app displays five households whose estimated stock portfolios beat the report’s SPY benchmark in both 2024 and 2025: Nancy Pelosi, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Tom Suozzi, Dwight Evans and Markwayne Mullin. Annual numbers are transcribed from Unusual Whales’ 2024 report and 2025 report; each card links the exact chart. These are approximate backtested stock portfolios, not audited accounts or returns achievable after disclosure. Two years of estimated outperformance is the inclusion rule, not proof of lasting skill. The 2025 benchmark is +16.8%. Coverage is limited to these selected households; hidden households do not count toward shared-buy flags. Profiles remain visible even when recent trades are absent from the latest feed. Annual roster evidence needs review when the next annual report is published; trade and price refresh remains automatic.

Imports

Import a CSV of disclosures you’ve checked. Imported rows and your watchlist stay in this browser on this device. Importing appends unique rows; it does not reconcile amendments automatically.

Price gain / loss

Yahoo Finance daily closes refresh automatically; the close date is shown on each row. The offline fallback was fetched September 26, 2026. Since trade = (latest close ÷ trade-day close − 1) × 100. Since disclosure uses the disclosed-day close instead. If that date or price is missing, the value is unavailable; no nearby trading date is silently substituted. Close prices are split-adjusted; dividends, fees and taxes are excluded. No intraday execution price is assumed. Options show the underlying stock change, not option returns; exercises use the exercise-day close, not the strike. This is a hypothetical holding-period price change, not verified politician profit or the return available after public disclosure. Price-source links and dates are in each trade. Missing data and sales display a dash. New price histories cover up to two years. Older or unresolved transactions may have no comparable price.

Shared buying flags

At least two distinct politician households purchasing the same ticker within the selected 7–90 day span, based on trade dates. Stocks, ADRs and calls count; sales, exercises, ETFs and other assets do not. Repeat trades and spouse/joint purchases count once per politician. Flags are ranked by buyer count, then newest trade date. Counts use the full loaded dataset, including labeled imports; table filters do not change them.

Each window’s first and last trade must fit the span; overlapping windows can appear separately. These are historical patterns in incomplete, delayed disclosures, not live alerts or a probability of insider information. Flags recalculate when new disclosures are loaded.

Read the dates and ownership

The disclosure gap counts calendar days from trade to the disclosed date. Congressional rows use their reported filing date; exact release times are unavailable. Executive signatures are labeled separately from publication dates. When publication is unknown, poor shows “Not supplied” instead of treating the signature as disclosure. This gap is not a legal lateness determination. Covered transactions generally must be reported within 30 days of notification and no later than 45 days after the transaction. House Ethics guidance ↗

Amounts are reported brackets, not execution prices or profits. Spouse, joint and self ownership remain distinct. Options and exercises are labeled separately from ordinary stock purchases.
